title: Horizon fusion batcher for streaming chat: KV-aware GPU budgeter
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Goal: implement a lightweight 'horizon fusion' batch formation heuristic optimized for streaming chat completions that balances GPU memory headroom and KV cache locality while preserving end-to-end latency SLOs. This ticket explores a hybrid trigger (time + size + kv-pressure) that fuses short-horizon windows of low-latency sessions into a micro-batch when KV cache reuse or GPU budget allows, and otherwise streams single-request paths. The heuristic must be pluggable, observable, and safe to roll back via rollout flags.

Motivation and constraints:
- Streaming chat traffic contains many short-turn bursts where merging a few turns increases throughput with negligible added latency if KV is hot.
- Aggressive merging risks KV inflation and premature GPU OOMs for long-context sessions.
- We need deterministic, debuggable rules for when to merge vs pass-through to keep tail latency predictable.

Design summary:
1) Horizon window: maintain a short sliding horizon (dynamic 5-40ms by default) per GPU slab to collect candidate requests. Horizon expands when observed intra-session KV hit-rate is above threshold and slab memory headroom > margin.
2) KV pressure score: combine per-session kv-size-estimate, recent cache-locality (hit-rate), and active-kv-residency to compute a normalized pressure metric. High pressure prevents fusion.
3) GPU budgeter: track ephemeral headroom per device (tokens in-flight, cached-kv-bytes, reserved batch reservations). Batcher only fuses if post-fusion budget < budget_limit. Budget_limit is configurable per tier.
4) Request affinity gating: prefer fusing requests with KV affinity (same session or high token-prefix overlap). Cross-session fusion allowed but only with cap to avoid cross-session KV churn.
5) Graceful fallback: on fusion failure (OOM or kernel allocation error), revert fused requests to passthrough and emit rollback metric and debug trace.

Trade-offs considered:
- Time-window vs predictive batching: we prefer small windows with KV-awareness to avoid building models that add complexity.
- Conservative defaults to protect SLOs; ops can open the window for dedicated capacity customers.
- We avoid cross-GPU fusion for now to limit complexity; future work could attempt inter-device batching with KV sharding.

Operational requirements:
- New metrics: horizon_fusions_total, horizon_fusion_failures, kv_pressure_distribution, fusion_latency_p50/p95, post-fusion_gpu_headroom.
- Trace context: attach fusion decision rationale to existing request traces for debugging.
- Config flags: enable_horizon_fusion (global), fusion_window_ms, kv_pressure_threshold, gpu_headroom_margin, cross_session_cap. All exposed in Console runtime config with defaults per tier.
acceptance_criteria: Horizon fusion enabled behind feature flag and default off for hosted-tier; on for dedicated with conservative defaults
Fusion reduces tokens-per-second cost by >=6% on internal chat workload A with no regression in p95 latency >10ms
No increase in OOM rate above noise (<=0.1% delta) during 72h canary on dedicated pool
All new metrics emitted and dashboards created; traces include fusion_decision tag
implementation_notes: Integrate with existing microbatch planner interface; add FusionCandidate struct with kv_estimate and affinity_score fields represented as ints to keep serialization cheap
Compute kv_estimate using existing kv-size estimator from ENG-64892; fall back to token-length heuristic when estimator is cold
Add GPU budgeter component that subscribes to slab allocator notifications and maintains a small moving-average headroom estimate
Keep fusion decision pure function of snapshot state to simplify unit testing and deterministic replay
Expose tuning knobs via runtime config and add guardrails for canary rollout
tests: Unit: fusion decision under varying kv_pressure and headroom scenarios (deterministic inputs)
Integration: local simulated streaming chat harness with mixed session lengths, assert p95 latency does not regress
Chaos: inject slab OOM on fused batch and verify rollback path and metrics
Performance: A/B run against internal chat load for 48h to measure cost delta and tail-latency impact
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal cluster dev-testing (flag on, no external traffic) for 3 days. Stage 2: dedicate canary pool with 5% traffic on dedicated customers for 72h. Stage 3: if canary OK, progressive ramp to 25% then 100% on dedicated; remain off for hosted until runtime-1.21 stabilization and PM approval. Emergency kill-switch will disable fusion globally. Post-rollout review after 7 days.
